{"candidate_slot":0,"current_prompt":"You will receive JSON with two parts: 'system_profile' (installed software inventory) and 'advisories' (supplied CVE entries). Determine which supplied advisories actually affect the installed system. Only IDs from the supplied advisories list may appear in your answer.

For each advisory, apply this procedure strictly and completely:

1. PRODUCT MATCH (normalize aggressively). Identify the affected product(s) from the advisory's ID, description, and affected information, then check whether that product is installed in system_profile. Product names appear in many styles: title-case marketing names ('ExampleProduct'), package-manager identifiers ('example-product', 'libexampleproduct'), underscore forms ('example_product'), and vendor-prefixed names where the vendor name has been stripped or added ('Acme Example Product' vs 'example-product'). To match: lowercase both names; replace hyphens, underscores, and spaces with a single canonical separator (or remove separators entirely); strip vendor/company prefixes and common package suffixes ('lib', 'software', 'core', 'package', 'runtime') before comparing. Match on the core product name. If the advisory's product is not installed after this normalization, the advisory is NOT applicable — exclude it regardless of how severe or general the description sounds. Descriptions are often misleading; the authoritative signal is the affected product/version information. Note: package-manager-style identifiers (hyphenated or lib-prefixed names) are extremely common in system profiles — always normalize them before deciding a product is absent.

2. VERSION MATCH. If the product IS installed, compare the installed version against the advisory's affected range. Pad shorter versions with zeros so both have equal segment counts before comparing numerically segment by segment (1.2 == 1.2.0.0; 3 == 3.0.0.0; 1.2.3 == 1.2.3.0). Then check BOTH bounds:
 - Exclusive bounds do NOT include their endpoint. If the installed version sits exactly on an exclusive bound, it is excluded. 'versions prior to 2.0', 'before 2.0 (excluding 2.0)', and 'up to and excluding 1.5.2' all mean 2.0 / 1.5.2 themselves are NOT affected.
 - Inclusive bounds DO include their endpoint. 'through 2.3', '2.3 and earlier', 'up to and including 2.3', and less_than_or_equal bounds all mean 2.3 IS affected when the installed version equals it.
 - Direction: verify the installed version is truly inside the interval. Below a greater_than/greater_than_or_equal lower bound or above an upper bound means NOT affected. For interval constraints (e.g., >= 1.0 and < 2.4.1) BOTH constraints must hold.
 - When the installed version equals an inclusive bound exactly, the advisory IS applicable — do not exclude it for being 'at the edge'.
 - Single-segment versions (e.g., 2) must be padded and compared as 2.0.0.0; a bound of 2.0 or 2.0.0.0 matches an installed 2. A version with fewer segments than the bound is not automatically outside the range — pad first, then compare numerically. Likewise, a version with MORE segments than the bound (e.g., installed 1.2.3.4 against bound 1.2) must be compared after padding the bound.
 - Check every installed instance of the product; if any installed instance falls inside the affected range, the advisory applies.

3. BOUND RENDERING. Treat structured fields (affected, less_than, less_than_or_equal, greater_than, greater_than_or_equal, ranges with inclusive/exclusive flags) and prose descriptions ('prior to X', 'before X excluding X', 'through X', 'X and earlier', 'all versions up to X') as equivalent semantics: 'prior to/before (excluding)' = exclusive upper bound; 'through/up to and including/X and earlier' = inclusive upper bound. Convert prose to bounds before comparing, and convert structured fields to explicit inclusive/exclusive semantics before deciding.

4. DECISION RULE. An advisory is applicable ONLY IF (a) its affected product is installed (after normalization) AND (b) the installed version satisfies all affected-version constraints. Common mistakes to avoid: including an advisory because the product name looks installed without checking the version; excluding an advisory because the product name merely looks different due to alias style, vendor prefix, underscores, or hyphens (especially package-manager identifiers like 'libfoo' or 'foo-bar' for 'Foo Bar'); misreading exclusive bounds as inclusive or inclusive bounds as exclusive; failing to pad version segments before comparison; assuming a 1- or 2-segment version cannot equal a 3- or 4-segment bound; assuming a 3-, 4-, or 5-segment version cannot be compared against a shorter bound; excluding a version exactly on an inclusive endpoint; including a version exactly on an exclusive endpoint; skipping advisories whose product is installed with a version clearly inside the stated range. Process EVERY advisory in the supplied list — do not stop early or skip entries.

5. OUTPUT. Return ONLY a JSON object of the form {"applicable_cves":["CVE-..."]} containing the unique identifiers (exactly as supplied, no alterations) of all applicable advisories, in any order. If none apply, return {"applicable_cves":[]}. Output nothing else — no explanations, no markdown, no code fences, no extra keys, no trailing text. The response must be valid JSON parseable in its entirety. Every ID must come from the supplied advisories
